newsitem.title: INDIA: India Power Grid seeks $150-200 mln external loans.
newsitem.headline: India Power Grid seeks $150-200 mln external loans.

text.p: India's state-run Power Grid Corp aims to borrow between $150 million to $200 million in the external market to fund an ambitious expansion plan, a senior company official said on Thursday.
Power Grid, which has a monopoly on power transmission, has invited offers for a first tranche of $50 million, Ramesh Bahri, Power Grid's deputy general manager for corporate planning, told Reuters.

"This is the first time we are entering the market. Bids (for syndication) were invited on the 30th of July," Bahri told Reuters by telephone. "We expect to raise $150 million to $200 million in tranches. The first tranche is for $50 million."
"It is for the bankers to assess Power Grid, but we expect the (interest) rate to be around 50 to 60 basis points over LIBOR." he said, referring to the London Interbank Offered Rate.

India's Disinvestment Commission, which advises the government on privatisation strategy, said in a report on Wednesday that it did not want any sale of state stakes in Power Grid for the time being as it was not ready for the market.

The commission said Power Grid had a high level of efficiency comparable with international transmission companies, but faced problems in realising its dues from state electricity boards (SEBs), which are in poor financial condition.

Strengthening India's transmission infrastructure needs an investment of 560 billion rupees ($15.7 billion), the panel said. "Power Grid would need to raise such resources from the market either through debt instruments or through equity issue," it said.

The government said last June that international financial institutions had committed 60 billion rupees ($1.68 billion) to finance new Power Grid projects, in addition to an equal amount already committed for ongoing projects.
The World Bank had agreed in principle to extend $1.2 bilion against a basket of projects spread over five to seven years, in addition to existing commitments worth $1.5 billion, it said.
Bahri said Power Grid planned to use its first tranche mainly to build transmission lines from a hydro-electric power project at Tehri in the northern state of Uttar Pradesh.
The firm expects to follow a market convention in seeking $50 million each in subsequent tranches, aiming to raise the funds once every three to four months, Bahri said.
Power Grid, which currently earns transmission charges calculated at 12 percent of its equity, has been demanding that the rate be raised to 16 percent.
The disinvestment panel said the power sector as a whole needed reforms and inability of electricty boards to impose price hikes on consumers was an area of concern for Power Grid.
"While the government is seized of the problems, it may take a few years before all the reforms are put in place and the system is given proper commercial and market orientation," it said.
A partial privatisation of Power Grid could wait until the changes are achieved in order to attract the right kind of response from investors, it said.

Power Grid, which has not officially published its financial figures for 1996/97 (April-March), is expected to show a net profit of 3.07 billion rupees ($86 million), compared with 2.76 billion in 1995/96, a company official said.
Turnover is expected at around 10.0 billion rupees ($280 million), up from 9.76 billion, he said. ($1=35.7 rupees)
